title: I Was Gone Eleven Minutes
evidence_boundary: This is a first-person account of a subjective psychedelic experience. It makes no claim that the entities encountered are real beings, that the experience revealed objective truths about reality, or that DMT is safe. Nothing here is medical advice or encouragement to use any substance.
desired_movement: From treating an ordinary room as the whole of reality to holding open the possibility that experience has rooms we do not normally enter - without claiming to know what they are.
grounding: The account returns to the ceiling, the fan, the friend's face, and the clock before its final line.
invitation: I don't know what it was. I'm not going to pretend I do.
end_card_question: What if this room isn't the whole building?
voice_standard: Liam - quiet testimony, like someone telling you at 2am and still a little shaken. Plain and grounded through the ordinary room, breathless and awed through the breakthrough, cracked and tender on the crying beat. Near-whisper on the final line. Never lecture, never explain - this is memory, not analysis.
